plant: ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel Anakapalle steel plant
evidence_note: The 8.2 is the environmental clearance. After the March foundation ceremony, ArcelorMittal called the project announced in both its June- and September-quarter results. Both steel sponsors are identified.

JSW identifies a 5 Mt/yr greenfield first phase. GEM lists 7 in converters and JSW lists a 6 Mt/yr melt shop. The approved site addition sets the cap. The September-quarter call confirms work on phase one, with phase two approved in October.

The three 2 Mt/yr converters match the disclosed site expansion from about 9 to 15. The earlier equipment-substitution proposal adds no separate tonnes. The joint venture owns the Indian business through a Luxembourg holding company.
Phase III takes the works from 10 to 15 Mt/yr. JSW documents converter installation. Blast-furnace iron capacity and rolling capacity are separate stages of the same works.

plant: Jindal Shadeed Iron & Steel Duqm plant
evidence_note: Jindal identifies 5 Mt/yr of direct-reduced iron and hot-briquetted iron. The equipment supplier describes two 2.5 Mt/yr ironmaking modules and provision for a future hot link to a melt shop. The zone calls the wider development a steel project. These disclosures do not establish 5 Mt/yr of crude-steel furnaces under construction.

GEM lists 3.5 Mt/yr under construction. The successor operator tendered a single electric furnace of up to 1.5 Mt/yr in April 2026. That procurement describes a materially different project and does not establish construction of the listed 3.5 Mt/yr.

Tata approved a broader 4.8 Mt/yr addition in July. Its September-quarter account describes roads, grading and equipment orders. The stage of the two GEM construction converters could not be reconciled. Tata had already bought the remaining minority stake in 2025.

plant: Tata Steel Port Talbot steel plant
evidence_note: Tata’s former integrated works had about 5 Mt/yr of capacity. Its two blast furnaces closed in 2024 as part of the conversion. The 3.2 Mt/yr electric furnace adds no capacity against that predecessor, even though the site stopped melting steel between the two routes.

plant: Makran Steel Sistan and Baluchestan Complex
evidence_note: The operator describes the three-million-tonne steel plant as a plan. Its reporting on ironmaking concerns a separate upstream plant. The steelmaking phase and amount under construction at the cutoff remain unconfirmed.

The record for Ohangwena traces its furnace construction and 3 Mt/yr rating to older capacity reports and sponsor posts. The project history gives a 2025 target start date. We could not establish the furnace’s September 2026 stage or a site-capacity increment from a contemporary project disclosure.

plant: Nucor Steel West Virginia steel plant
evidence_note: Nucor made the first heat at the new West Virginia sheet mill in September. The melt shop has two electric furnaces. The disclosure does not identify how much furnace capacity still counted as under construction at the cutoff.

The investor describes staged development, financing and a final investment decision, with separate electric furnaces for the two phases. Project approval and the stated target for hot-rolled coil do not establish that 3 Mt/yr of crude-steel capacity was under construction in September.

The existing Pesquería rolling mill uses purchased or imported slabs. Ternium reports that a new 2.6 Mt/yr electric steel shop and slab caster were being built there in the September quarter. The separate 2.1 Mt/yr direct-reduced iron module is outside the steel total.

plant: Zhenshi Group Eastern Special Steel Co Ltd
operator: Zhenshi Group EASTERN SPECIAL Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: The project environmental assessment assigns capacity rights from existing Jiaxing steelmaking and from previously retired Hangzhou steelworks. An old permit credit and a currently producing furnace give different baselines for physical capacity. The full furnace sum is not a verified net gain.

GEM links the two units to an earlier planned build. The operator group has several businesses at Jamuria. The available compliance filing covers a differently named 1 Mt/yr project and cannot confirm this 2.5 Mt/yr package at the cutoff.
POSCO marked completion of the 2.5 Mt/yr Gwangyang electric furnace in June 2026, before the September snapshot.

SSAB lists 2.3 Mt/yr of crude-steel capacity at the existing Luleå works. The 2.5 Mt/yr mill under construction replaces the entire blast-furnace-based production system. The increase over the pre-conversion site is 0.2 Mt/yr.

The first phase of Stegra’s new Boden works is sized at 2.5 Mt/yr of steel. The company’s 30 September update confirms construction continued after its ownership change. Its equity financing notice names investors without a complete stake breakdown.

HBIS’s securities filing identifies a 1.25-to-1 replacement ratio. Its 11.52 Mt/yr Laoting project, including the 230-tonne converter in phase two, consumes 14.41 Mt/yr in capacity rights from other group works. The in-construction unit adds capacity at Laoting while using existing domestic capacity rights.

plant: Huangshi Xingang Heavy Industry Technology Co Ltd
operator: Huangshi Xingang Heavy Industry Technology Co Ltd
evidence_note: The municipal permit names six electric furnaces at three Hubei producers with 2.30 Mt/yr to be withdrawn. The project uses 2.25 Mt/yr of those rights for its 2.25 Mt/yr at Huangshi. It adds local steelmaking while adding no permitted capacity across the linked Chinese sites.

plant: Xingtai Iron and Steel Co Ltd Weixian
operator: Xingtai Iron and Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: The relocation plan for the new Weixian site matches three 100-tonne electric furnaces totaling 2.25 Mt/yr to 2.25 Mt/yr from the old Xingtai site. The former works closed in September 2026. The relocation adds local capacity at Weixian and no capacity across the two Chinese sites.

operator: Kaptan Demir Celik Endustrisi Ve Ticaret AŞ
evidence_note: The Australian Anti-Dumping Commission verified the existing Marmara Ereğlisi electric melt shop and approximately 1.4 million tons of annual billet production. That output figure cannot establish what rated capacity would retire when the GEM construction furnace opens.

plant: Xuan Thien Nghia Hung steel plant
evidence_note: Vietnam’s government records a June 2025 groundbreaking for the multiproject Nam Định complex. A ceremony for the whole complex does not establish the physical stage of GEM’s particular steel furnace at the September cutoff.

operator: Henan Xinjinhui Stainless Steel Industry Co Ltd
evidence_note: The municipal government describes the stainless-steel project as an equal-capacity replacement of 2 Mt/yr. Against its designated predecessor capacity, this project adds no permitted crude-steel capacity. The project plan does not establish the exact date each old furnace stopped.

plant: Qinyang Hongda Iron & Steel Co Ltd
operator: Qinyang Hongda Iron & Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: The company profile identifies 0.5 Mt/yr of existing steelmaking and 1.2 Mt/yr of rolling. The sources checked do not reconcile that baseline with GEM’s separate 2 Mt/yr electric-furnace construction entry.

The European Commission’s approval for SALCOS Stage I explicitly leaves crude-steel capacity unchanged. The new 1.9 Mt/yr route replaces existing production. Salzgitter reported ongoing construction in its September-quarter report.

The second electric furnace produced its first heat on 9 October. The conversion replaces the coal-based route. Algoma’s investment decision compares 2.8 million tons of effective integrated capacity with 3.7 million tons after conversion, while its securities filing gives 3.6 million net tons of nameplate capacity for the former oxygen shop. Those baselines imply materially different additions.

Ecolant describes a new works in Vyksa designed to produce 1.8 Mt/yr of liquid steel for slab and round billet. The project’s July 2026 construction update targeted opening in the fourth quarter. Upstream direct-reduced iron is excluded.

plant: AG der Dillinger Hüttenwerke Dillingen steel plant
evidence_note: The Power4Steel project substitutes two electric furnaces across Dillingen and Völklingen for existing production. The beneficiaries committed to keeping their combined crude-steel capacity at 6 Mt/yr. The Dillingen installation therefore contributes no net capacity across the linked works.

The first Donawitz furnace under construction is rated at 0.85 Mt/yr, versus 1.7 in GEM. An additional expansion was subject to funding in June. The linked integrated route is being retired in stages. Neither the full 1.7 nor the initial 0.85 is established as a net addition.

plant: Tangshan Fengnan District Jing an Iron and Steel Co Ltd
operator: Tangshan Fengnan District Jing'an Iron and Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: The operator’s public environmental notice identifies the 160-tonne converter as a capacity-reducing replacement for two converters (120 and 60 tonnes) at the same site. Its stated annual liquid-steel output is 1.6 Mt, versus the 1.7 Mt/yr in GEM. Neither figure represents expansion.

Baosteel’s investment filing specifies 1.667 Mt/yr of crude steel, alongside separate iron and plate capacities. In May 2026 the sponsor said it would reassess timing and risks. The available sponsor disclosures establish the equity split but leave the physical furnace stage at the cutoff open.

plant: Tangshan Donghua Iron and Steel Enterprise Group Co Ltd
operator: Tangshan Donghua Iron & Steel Enterprise Group Co Ltd
evidence_note: The project moves capacity from Chunxing Special Steel to Donghua. Under the provincial plan, the two 110-tonne electric furnaces (1.65 Mt/yr combined) require 1.25 tonnes of withdrawn converter capacity for each new tonne. Separate adjustments to two converters at Donghua use their own allocations.

plant: Shanxi Zhongsheng Iron and Steel Co Ltd
operator: Shanxi Zhongsheng Iron and Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: Shanxi’s environmental approval requires two existing 60-tonne converters to be dismantled as the new 155-tonne converter is built. The permit documents the replacement but gives no like-for-like annual capacity figures for those old units.

plant: Wuzhou Yongda Iron and Steel Co Ltd
operator: Wuzhou Yongda Steel Works Co Ltd
evidence_note: The Guangxi replacement ledger retires 1.6477 Mt/yr of rights at Yongda’s existing works for three electric furnaces totaling 1.645 Mt/yr. The operator also describes existing company steel capacity of 1.645 Mt/yr.

The 1.6 Mt/yr electric furnace is part of a route conversion. The company describes linked blast-furnace retirements but does not give a comparable site-level crude-steel before-and-after series in the cited disclosures.

plant: Maanshan Iron and Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: The issuer’s exchange filing describes two 1.6 Mt/yr converters, one in each phase. Together they replace 4 Mt/yr across four Maanshan and two Baosteel Special Steel furnaces. The second phase cannot be counted as a separate increase in Chinese capacity.

plant: Henan Jiyuan Iron and Steel Group Co Ltd
operator: Henan Jiyuan Iron & Steel (Group) Co Ltd
evidence_note: The replacement schedule gives the combined steelmaking project 1.60 Mt/yr. It draws on 1.61 Mt/yr of converted predecessor capacity. The sponsor cannot add the full replacement converter and electric furnace to the old works’ capacity.

plant: Henan Yaxin Iron and Steel Group Co Ltd
operator: Henan YAXIN Steel Industry Co Ltd
evidence_note: The 1.6 Mt/yr converter replaces capacity from the Yaxin/Boxin combination and rights from Huixin Special Steel. The published ratios require 1.25 or 1.5 tonnes withdrawn for each new tonne.

Daric’s 2018 catalogue identifies the 1.5 Mt/yr billet furnace and a separate 1.5 Mt/yr sponge-iron unit. GEM’s subsequent dossier says the expansion disappeared from the company website in 2026 and interprets that as a cancellation. Neither source dates a formal cancellation or establishes furnace construction in September.

Danieli identifies the new Celaya furnace as a replacement for EAF No. 2 and expects faster production. Its scope gives no comparable before-and-after annual steelmaking capacities. The 1.5 Mt/yr in GEM cannot all be counted as added capacity.

DEACERO puts the addition to installed capacity from its new Ramos II steelworks at 1 Mt/yr. Equipment supplier Danieli rates the full minimill at 1.5. In early November Danieli reported that the new furnace was still being commissioned, with the old furnace supplying the first billet cast on the new line. Count the operator’s incremental capacity.

HyIron identifies the first Oshivela phase as 15,000 tonnes of direct-reduced iron per year and the next phase as an ironmaking expansion. These documents do not establish construction of the 1.5 Mt/yr steel furnace carried in GEM.

plant: Mount Zynai Zamboanga Sibugay steel plant
evidence_note: The Philippine Information Agency reported the industrial park inauguration in 2022. Two years later the mines bureau still listed Mount Zynai’s iron-processing permit application for the 14.83-hectare Diplahan site as under review. Neither record verifies work on a 1.5 Mt/yr steel furnace by September 2026.

Danieli’s order specified a new electric furnace and 1.46 Mt/yr of billets, blooms and beam blanks. Its original 2024 start date passed. The owner’s later project description tracks the rail and beam rolling mill, without establishing the stage of the new furnace in September.

SSAB lists 1.5 Mt/yr of existing crude-steel capacity at Oxelösund. The 1.5 Mt/yr electric furnace replaces the existing integrated steelmaking route. Installation was in progress in the September quarter.

plant: Shams Iron and Steel Complex Tabriz
evidence_note: Daric’s 2018 catalogue describes a new 1.5 Mt/yr steel shop at Ajabshir and a separate ironmaking unit of equal size. Its website still carried that description in 2024. Those records establish the design but leave an eight-year gap between the catalogue and the snapshot.

The provincial environmental permit explicitly describes the 1.4333 Mt/yr converter as a capacity-reducing replacement. Most existing equipment is to be dismantled. Daye’s March 2026 programme identifies the upgrade as ongoing.

plant: Yunnan Qujing Iron and Steel Group Yanggang Iron and Steel Co Ltd
operator: Yunnan Qujing Iron and Steel Group Yanggang Iron and Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: The project assessment identifies a 1.4 Mt/yr converter as part of a wider group transformation under a replacement plan. It says the previous approval did not allocate each withdrawn unit’s capacity among individual projects. No separate net increment can be assigned to this converter.

plant: Meghna Re-rolling and Steel Mills steel plant
operator: Meghna Re-rolling and Steel Mills Ltd
evidence_note: IFC identifies a new 1.4 Mt/yr melt shop and 0.9 Mt/yr rolling mill. A June 2026 site visit and interviews with Meghna officials found the steel factory built and waiting for a gas connection. Its 1.4 Mt/yr stays in the September tracker total. It contributes zero to the checked total for construction still active that month.

plant: Tangshan Ganglu Iron and Steel Co Ltd
operator: Tangshan Ganglu Iron & Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: Hebei’s approval identifies the 1.35 Mt/yr converter as part of the Ganglu consolidation. Its required replacement ratios of 1.25 or 1.5 to one mean retiring more capacity than the project installs.

plant: Rizhao Steel Holding Group Co Ltd
operator: Rizhao Steel Holding Group Co Ltd
evidence_note: Shandong’s phase-two ledger lists the 1.35 Mt/yr converter. It applies a 1.1-to-1 reduction for internal and merged capacity and 1.25-to-1 for purchased rights. The furnace adds capacity at its destination while using a larger volume of existing domestic rights.

plant: Hebei Mingbin Iron and Steel Co Ltd
operator: Hebei New Wuan Steel Group Wenan IRON&STEEL Co Ltd
evidence_note: The provincial consolidation notice covers a 1.35 Mt/yr converter under Puyang and Wen’an. The national inspection identified disagreements over historical capacity credits at several Handan works. These records do not independently establish a separate September net increase under the Mingbin project ID.

operator: DST Nghi Son Iron and Steel JSC
evidence_note: Thanh Hóa’s investment approval assigns 0.98 Mt/yr to a scrap-to-hot-coil line and 0.33 Mt/yr to downstream products. Their sum matches the tracker’s 1.31 Mt/yr. In August 2026 the province was still arranging resettlement for eight households. Neither document establishes a separate furnace rating and physical furnace construction by September.

plant: Shougang Qian an Iron and Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: The Hebei permit allocates 1.95 Mt/yr from the existing 210-tonne converter to a 1.30 Mt/yr electric furnace. In November, after the September snapshot, the province confirmed the completed replacement matched the approved plan.

plant: Jahan Foolad Sirjan Steel Kerman plant
evidence_note: Jahan Foolad identifies its first electric furnace as a 1 Mt/yr billet plant opened in 2019. Its project catalogue lists a second steelmaking plant with a different rating from the tracker’s 1.3 Mt/yr. The catalogue gives no dated construction milestone that would establish which capacity was being installed in September.

Nigeria’s steel ministry describes a technical and financial audit to decide how to revive the existing Ajaokuta works. That assessment supplies neither evidence of active converter construction in September nor a quantified increase over the original plant design.

Danieli’s order documents the Mirsarai minimill. In September the sponsor’s chief operating officer said work had reached roughly halfway before loan disbursements stopped and equipment was held at port. The available disclosure does not establish how far the steelmaking furnace itself had advanced or whether work on it continued at the cutoff.

plant: Baotou Deshun Special Steel Co Ltd
operator: Baotou Deshun Spec. Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: The planned 1.25 Mt/yr converter formed part of a merger and relocation with Baotou Jiyu. A November 2026 provincial notice proposed transferring capacity away from both named operators. That later notice prevents treating the tracked project as a confirmed September net addition.

GEM flags 1.243 Mt/yr of induction capacity. The site's earlier compliance return already records billet production and operating consent for 0.7714 Mt/yr of billets. The remaining crude-steel increment cannot be matched unit by unit. Ownership also passes through several private entities.

plant: Guangxi Liugang Zhongjin Stainless Steel Co Ltd
operator: Guangxi Liugang Zhongjin Stainless Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: The 2025 bond rating report distinguishes existing stainless-steel melting capacity of 1.53 Mt/yr from hot rolling of 1.20 Mt/yr. It does not show a separate 1.20 Mt/yr crude-steel addition. The listed construction capacity therefore remains unresolved.

During a July 2026 site visit, the head of Iran’s mining development agency reported that about 80% of the equipment was installed and identified 1.2 Mt/yr as the capacity for steel sheet. The report gives no separate rating or installation milestone for the electric steelmaking furnace.

The environmental hearing notice describes 1.2 Mt/yr of rebar and wire rod and a scrap-recycling minimill. SteelAsia describes its Concepcion investment as forthcoming. These disclosures do not identify 1.2 Mt/yr of independently verified melting capacity under construction in September.

Almaty’s regional government announced a November 2025 foundation ceremony for a new plant with melting furnaces and 1.2 Mt/yr of steel capacity. In July 2026 the regional investment council still described construction as starting that year and gave capacities for rolled products. September progress on the melting unit remains unresolved.

operator: Fujian Yixin Steel & Iron Co Ltd
evidence_note: The company’s old and new oxygen furnaces are identified in the local plan and an exchange filing. Two existing 45-tonne converters representing 1.6 Mt/yr were to be withdrawn for one 100-tonne converter. The older filing rates it at 1.2 Mt/yr and the municipal plan at 1.15. Both fall below the predecessor capacity.

plant: Henan Fengbao Special Steel Co Ltd
operator: Henan Fengbao SPECIAL Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: The provincial project table specifies a 1.5-to-1 replacement ratio for the 1.15 Mt/yr converter, requiring the project to surrender more existing steelmaking capacity than it builds.

plant: Zunyi Fuxin Special Steel Equipment Manufacturing Co Ltd
operator: Zunyi County Fuxin Iron & Steel Product Co Ltd
evidence_note: Two new electric furnaces total 1.11 Mt/yr. Guizhou’s approval identifies two old furnaces totaling 1.15 Mt/yr at the same site and the rights allocated from them. The province’s investment list confirms the same equipment scope.

ArcelorMittal is converting the long-products steelmaking route for its existing rail and wire-rod mills. The new furnace is sized at 1.1 Mt/yr of semis. The sponsor does not quantify a like-for-like increase across the connected Asturias works.

SteelAsia identifies a steelmaking line and a rolling line at Lemery. Its published rating of 500,000 tonnes is for beam and other steel products. The separate 1.1 Mt/yr crude-steel increment in GEM remains unconfirmed.

plant: Lloyds Metals and Energy Ltd Ghugus steel plant
evidence_note: Lloyds documents construction of a new steelmaking operation at its ironmaking site. Use GEM's 1.05 Mt/yr of steelmaking furnaces. The 1.2 Mt/yr long-products project has a different equipment boundary.
The Uzbek presidency records commissioning of the new casting and rolling complex in July 2026. The equipment supplier identifies its electric melt shop as part of the same minimill contract.

plant: Chongqing Zuhang Iron and Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: The municipal authority inspected the new 1.01 Mt/yr furnace and the removal of two furnaces with the same combined capacity in June 2026. Both the replacement and its completion predate the September snapshot.

plant: Zarand Iranian Steel Company Kerman plant
evidence_note: A project-control engineer working for MIDHCO’s engineering arm describes a 2022 expansion plan for a 1 Mt/yr electric steel plant and a separate 1.5 Mt/yr iron-reduction unit. The account gives no date for installing the electric furnace or any change to the existing steelworks’ capacity by September 2026.

Sirjan Iranian Steel identifies an existing 1 Mt/yr billet plant at Bardsir. A company manager described direct reduction as the expansion then under construction and steelmaking as a later step. These records do not confirm a second 1 Mt/yr steelmaking furnace under construction in September 2026.

plant: African Natural Resources and Mines Kaduna steel plant
evidence_note: The operator identifies the Gujeni plant’s product as direct-reduced iron for use in steelmaking. The group also sells rebar. Neither activity identifies an on-site crude-steel furnace with 1 Mt/yr of additional capacity under construction in September.

plant: Unitex Steel Mills Feni steel plant
evidence_note: The equipment supplier contracted to build a new minimill in Feni and originally scheduled startup for 2024. Its order does not establish whether the new furnace was under construction in September 2026.

SteelAsia’s engineering contract and product target establish a project at Candelaria. The public materials describe heavy sections and do not independently date the start of physical construction of the steelmaking furnace or establish its incremental liquid-steel rating.

The project’s investment group documented excavation, reinforcing steel and concrete for a new melt shop at Qorveh before the cutoff. It assigns 1 Mt/yr to hot-rolled sheet from the integrated mill. Its description gives no separate annual capacity for the furnace, so the exact crude-steel addition remains open.

plant: Fujian Fuhua New Materials Group Co Ltd
operator: Mindong Saiqi Economic Development Zone Fuhua Steel Rolling Co Ltd
evidence_note: Fujian revoked the 0.825 Mt/yr Ningde scheme in August 2026 after the sponsors confirmed it had not been implemented. The original project would have reused capacity from two local electric furnaces.

GEM separately lists 0.206 Mt/yr already operating. The state consent covering April 2025 to March 2027 lists five induction furnaces with 0.539 Mt/yr. The permits and GEM records do not identify the same outstanding set of furnaces.

plant: Miyaneh Steel East Azerbaijan steel plant
evidence_note: Mianeh is building its first electric melt shop alongside its iron-reduction plant. The project engineer specifies 0.8 Mt/yr of billets, and SMS Concast identifies the melt shop as new. The operator tested the ladle furnace in February 2026 and was still preparing the steelmaking line for startup in October. The new shop adds 0.8 Mt/yr.

At the April 2026 annual meeting, the chief executive reported an operating direct-reduction plant rated at 0.8 Mt/yr and a cold-briquetting plant rated at 0.072 Mt/yr. An earlier OECD inventory separately listed a 0.8 Mt/yr electric steelmaking furnace as under way. The two figures for iron and steel describe different units. The meeting report gives no construction milestone for the furnace.

plant: Xinjiang Tianshan Iron and Steel Bazhou Co Ltd
operator: Xinxing Ductile Iron Pipes Xinjiang Co Ltd
evidence_note: The regional development commission describes a 100-tonne electric furnace and strip-casting line at an existing industrial site. It quotes 0.5 Mt/yr for the line. The scope differs from GEM’s 0.75 Mt/yr furnace entry, and the cited disclosure gives no before-and-after crude-steel capacity.
Tata inaugurated its electric arc furnace in March and reported ramping up production in July. Its 0.75 Mt/yr falls outside the September construction cohort.

Shakhty’s industrial history records a 0.73 Mt/yr steelworks on this site before the Donelektrostal investment. The regional investment agency described plans for an electric melt shop and rolling equipment. The project records do not show which existing furnaces would remain, or what crude-steel capacity the site would gain over its former rating.

operator: GV do Brasil Industria e Comercio de Aço Ltda
evidence_note: Grupo Simec reports 0.52 Mt/yr of existing billet capacity at Pindamonhangaba at the end of 2025. Its filing also describes construction of a steel shop and a rolling mill and gives a 0.50 Mt/yr production objective. It does not reconcile the new steel rating with the existing billet capacity or with GEM’s 0.70 Mt/yr record.

The site is being revived. Ramsarup describes a 0.70 Mt/yr billet shop under implementation. The dated May 2026 approval is for a specialty bar mill with a furnace. It does not establish how much of the older electric steelmaking project was under construction in September.

plant: Gulf Tubing Company Ras Al-Khair steel plant
evidence_note: Gulf Tubing specifies 0.63 Mt/yr of steel billets for the proposed Ras Al-Khair tube works. Its project schedule refers to construction design starting in 2018. A dated September 2026 furnace construction milestone is missing.

plant: Sarmad Iron and Steel Complex Abarkouh
operator: Sarmad Iron and Steel Complex Abarkouh
evidence_note: Sarmad describes construction of a new electric melt shop and billet caster to supply its existing rolling mill. The operator rates the addition at 0.6 Mt/yr and records equipment installation. On 7 September 2026 it invited bids for the steelmaking project's water-supply system. The separate direct-reduction and rolling projects add no crude-steel tonnes to this figure.

Sri Lanka’s Board of Investment records a land allocation and a foundation ceremony at Mirijjawila in 2022. Its report distinguishes the earlier cement plant on that stretch of land. It gives no date for furnace installation or verified steelmaking capacity under construction in September 2026.
Commercial Metals placed its Berkeley County micromill in service during its fiscal fourth quarter ending August 31. It falls outside September construction.

An earlier application raised crude-steel capacity from 0.127 to 0.681 Mt/yr, matching the GEM increment. A later application instead describes a smaller phase reaching 0.289. The date and extent of the larger construction phase remain unresolved.

Daric’s 2018 catalogue identifies 0.55 Mt/yr of billets and blooms from an electric furnace at Saeb, alongside a separate ironmaking plant. The design matches GEM’s rating. The catalogue supplies no September 2026 construction milestone.

The OECD listed a proposed 0.55 Mt/yr electric furnace at Arian Steel in 2024, with no start year. The company identifies its sections and rebar business at the Eshtehard–Bouin Zahra site. Those records establish the proposed furnace size and the existing products but leave construction progress and retirements unresolved in September 2026.

Amir Kabir Khazar describes an ingot shop and three direct-reduction units in its design for Arak. On the same page it reports construction of a separate billet plant in Rasht. The Rasht progress cannot establish the stage of the Arak steel furnace in September 2026.

plant: Yunnan Tiangao Nickel Alloy Co Ltd
operator: YunNan Province Tiangao Nickel Alloy Co Ltd
evidence_note: The municipal inspection identifies preconstruction approvals for a transformation of the existing works. The existing furnace list and transformation plan do not establish that the 0.5 Mt/yr in GEM is an incremental September addition.

Baobab's directors signed accounts on 11 August 2026 that describe an ongoing search for investors to develop Tete. The company's feasibility study sized a proposed mill at 0.5 Mt/yr. The financing record and the study establish the plan but leave the start of furnace construction unresolved.

Ittehad reports 0.5 Mt/yr across its Faisalabad and Islamabad plants combined. It describes the planned increase to 1 Mt/yr as an expansion of bar finishing. Neither figure identifies a new 0.5 Mt/yr induction furnace at Faisalabad or a net increase in crude-steel capacity there.

Pakistan’s CPEC Secretariat documented construction at Rashakai in 2021. In December 2024 the planning ministry was still trying to resolve land prices and electricity tariffs with the company. The records identify the investment and early construction but leave the first 0.5 Mt/yr phase’s furnace status unresolved in September 2026.

plant: Thai Nguyen Iron and Steel plant
operator: Thai Nguyen Iron And Steel JSC
evidence_note: TISCO reports that work on its Phase II expansion stopped in 2013. Its board sought termination of the engineering and construction contract, and on 6 October 2026 the operator and provincial authorities were still reviewing obstacles to the project. The suspended 0.5 Mt/yr falls outside active September construction.

Daric’s 2018 catalogue lists 0.5 Mt/yr of steel billets from an electric furnace separately from 0.5 Mt/yr of rolling capacity at Sabalan. The figures describe one chain of production, and the historical catalogue does not verify construction eight years later.

operator: Jinzhou Jinxing Special Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: Liaoning approved a 0.36 Mt/yr electric furnace using 0.38 Mt/yr of retiring converter capacity. The linked permit provides no increase in crude-steel capacity.

Beltrame acquired the former COS works with an 80-tonne electric furnace and two rolling lines. The issuer describes a future greenfield investment separately from the rolling restart. The September crude-steel construction stage and any increase over the predecessor melt shop cannot be reconciled from these sources.

GEM lists an additional electric arc furnace. JSW reports current capacity of 0.95 Mt/yr and identifies a structural rolling mill in its expansion programme. The site's future crude-steel increment is unconfirmed.
Gerdau reported an expansion of 150,000 tonnes of annual crude-steel capacity at its existing Texas works. Its September-quarter results describe work in progress.

plant: Yunnan Qujing Shuangyou Iron and Steel Co Ltd
operator: Yunnan Qujing Shuangyou Iron and Steel Co Ltd
evidence_note: The assessment describes 1.30 Mt/yr of steel across the upgraded works, ten times the 0.13 in GEM’s construction row. Qujing’s January 2026 inspection verifies one old converter retired under the group’s capacity-neutral project. The sources do not match the tracker’s smaller figure to a distinct net addition.

North Korea's state news agency reported installation work on a new electric furnace in August 2024. Its 3 September 2026 report on Chollima gives no annual steel capacity for that unit. The report’s tonnage refers to an electrode production base. Gross and net furnace capacity remain unknown.
